claim_under_test: 'After he does them at least once he would learn all of those permanently, so we solve everything on a computer.' Prior rounds measured the RATE of one-shot generalisation. This round asks about the PRICE, and about whether the learned thing is even written in the language the acting half reads.
corrections: The hypothesis that a small shared vocabulary would saturate was tested and is FALSE: the second half of experience added 57% of the final vocabulary.

An empty description is not evidence the page cannot name an element. 318 elements have no text and no id and are named correctly by class and order; reporting them as 3.32-bit ambiguity was my language's silence, not the page's.

More predicates do not make a description cheaper: median 27 survivors with one property vs 63 with two, because the recorded count is over syntactic descriptions, many of which select the same element.

external_confirmation_fetched_2026_11_16.BEPA (arXiv 2601.05787): names the same defect: expert traces 'often operate in tool-level action spaces that a single end-to-end policy cannot directly imitate' -- structural mismatch between what was demonstrated and what can be acted on
external_confirmation_fetched_2026_11_16.DOM vs Screenshots (2026): 'hybrid agents lose grounding when their two channels disagree about which element is the same element', and 'accessibility-tree agents lose grounding when a page rerenders a list and element indices reshuffle mid-task' -- exactly the finding that ordinals are 95%, not 100%, stable
external_confirmation_fetched_2026_11_16.GUI-Primitives (EMNLP 2026): list ordinal is understood at 0.82-0.90 conditional on a correct candidate, so position is a real identity signal, and 'most failures reflect candidate localization'

honest_limits: AUTHORITY NONE -- one producer run in one sandbox.
Part 1 and 2 READ a recorded run; they are not a new experiment and say so.
The 0.929-bit figure is for elements the page's own properties name; it does not claim a pixel-only surface can be named this way, and does not cover canvas or remote-desktop surfaces.
one_description_language_v1 is a SIGNATURE, not a judge: it says which elements are indistinguishable, never which is correct. instruction_contract_v1 still decides, unchanged.
Ordinal stability was measured on 5 pages x 5 seeds; 12 of 241 descriptions changed, so a stored ordinal without its peer-count would be a silent wrong answer.
Nothing is credited: no capability, weight, terminal or family-rank claim.
laws: The thing that acts and the thing that learns must describe the element the same way, or experience is written in a language nothing reads.
One experience is one bit; a step costs 5.43. That is arithmetic about what one observation separates, not a shortcoming of the learner.
The price of a description is log2 of the descriptions that still fit, so the only lever that lowers it is REMOVING descriptions -- never more pages.
A description that cannot report how many other elements it also selects cannot report its own price.
An ordinal is stable only while its peer-count is; store the count or do not store the ordinal.

part_1_the_price.what_one_experience_pays: about one bit, because each description is struck out or not by a binary question

part_3_the_two_languages.acting: instruction_policy_v1 -> instruction_contract_v1 + anchored_frame_v1 -> an element INDEX
part_3_the_two_languages.learning: demonstration_version_space_v1 -> its own private tuple grammar
part_3_the_two_languages.measurement: 1415 actionable elements on 130 real pages: 946 (66.9%) named to exactly one element by a description; 318 have neither own words nor an id (class + order names them); 151 have a name that repeats (order separates the twins); mean bits 0.929 vs 5.428 for the learner

ordinal_stability.consequence: an ordinal is stored WITH its peer-count, or it is not stored
ordinal_stability.why_they_change: peer count differs per instance (email-inbox rows 5/6/10)

the_wrong_answer_this_replaces: 'Learning is weak, so learn more.' The learner is not weak. What was wrong is that a learned description and an acted index are two vocabularies, so experience bought bits in a currency the action path never cashes.
